title: Same-arch stopped continuation primitive
goal: Implement one narrow machinen move continuation primitive for a same-architecture stopped single-thread process, with reexec/restart/resource reconstruction banned and fail-closed refusals for all unmodeled state.
problemStatement: machinen move currently refuses because no supported path proves modeled live-state continuation without falling back to reexec or reconstruction.
solutionStatement: Deliver a narrow proof-backed continuation primitive that resumes captured live process state only for an exact safe shape and refuses every unsupported shape without starting a target process.
technicalStatement: Define a same-arch stopped-process safe-point contract, capture registers/memory/mappings/resource state, materialize target-native state, resume from that state, and add guardrails proving no reexec or restart path is used.

tasks.title: Define exact continuation contract
tasks.problemStatement: A continuation primitive is unsafe unless the exact supported process shape and non-claims are written before implementation.
tasks.solutionStatement: Create a small contract for a same-arch stopped single-thread safe-point process and list every required captured live-state field and refusal class.
tasks.technicalStatement: Document a machine-readable and human-readable contract covering source shape, register state, memory mappings, stack, file descriptors, signals, timers, sockets, active syscalls, target architecture, and product-claim status.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the contract defines the exact supported source shape, including same architecture, single thread, stopped user-mode safe point, no active syscall, stable executable/text identity, modeled private memory, and no unmodeled fds/sockets/timers/signals/session state.
proofChecklist.evidence: Created docs/snapshot/same-arch-stopped-continuation-primitive-contract.json and docs/snapshot/same-arch-stopped-continuation-primitive.md. The contract defines the exact supported shape: same architecture arm64-to-arm64 or amd64-to-amd64, single thread, move-owned stopped user-mode safe point, no active syscall, stable executable/text identity, captured private writable mappings/stack/registers/TLS, inert stdio only, and refusals for non-stdio fds, sockets, timers, signals, terminal/session state, ambiguous mappings, and identity gaps. Validation command python3 -m json.tool passed in 0.05s, and the contract phrase check passed in 0.02s with required=21, missing=[], refusalClasses=14.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the contract states all hard bans: no reexec, restart, static-root reconstruction, output replay, descriptor-only equivalence, app export/import, source-ISA emulation, source-fd teleportation, metadata-only success, broad runtime support, or product claim without actual continuation proof.
proofChecklist.evidence: The same contract and Markdown explicitly list hardBans for reexec, restart, static-root reconstruction, output replay, descriptor-only equivalence, app export/import, source-ISA emulation, source-fd teleportation, metadata-only success, runtime-profile shortcut, broad runtime support, arbitrary process restore, active session migration without an explicit model, and product claim without actual continuation proof. The targetContinuationStep has mustNotExecArgv=true and success evidence must show no target-original, target-native-reexec, generic-resource-graph-reexec, static HTTP, file cursor, pipe replay, or resource reconstruction loader was invoked. The phrase check verified all required hard-ban phrases were present.

tasks.title: Materialize and resume target state
tasks.problemStatement: A continuation primitive is not proven until the target process resumes from captured live state rather than starting from argv.
tasks.solutionStatement: Materialize target-native process state and resume at the captured safe point without invoking a reexec or restart loader.
tasks.technicalStatement: Implement a target continuation path that writes modeled memory/register state into a target process, verifies text/mapping identity, resumes execution from the captured program counter, and reports targetPid only after resume succeeds.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the happy path resumes from captured live state and observes post-resume behavior that could not be produced by a fresh restart from argv alone.
proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented materializeSameArchStoppedContinuationTarget() in packages/runtime/src/same-arch-stopped-continuation.ts. The focused Vitest happy path passed in 0.57s and proves an eligible capture can be materialized as state=ready only when target text identity is verified, captured memory is materialized, registers are installed, target preflight has no refused resource, targetPid is present, and the continuation marker is captured-state-dependent with observedValue=42 while freshRestartWouldProduce=1. The ready result reports resumedFromCapturedState=true, targetProcessStarted=true, targetPid=7001, and all shortcut flags reexecUsed/restartUsed/resourceReconstructionUsed=false.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove no target reexec/restart/resource-reconstruction loader is called on the continuation path and no target process remains running on refusal.
proofChecklist.evidence: The same focused Vitest run passed in 0.57s and proves materialization refuses reexecAttempted, restartAttempted, resourceReconstructionAttempted, missing text identity, missing memory materialization, missing registers, target resource preflight refusal, missing targetPid, metadata-only marker, fresh-start-equivalent marker, and pre-refused capture classification.
